subject: Numeracy
title: One more
subtopics: One more in stories and songs
objectives: Children will add one more object to a small group.
Children will say or show how many there are now, with support.
content: Adding one more object to a small group and saying how many there are now, using objects, fingers and stories.
teachingActivities: Count the group first, add one object slowly, say "one more", and recount from one; keep groups to one to four.
learnerActivities: Add one more to a group, recount, show the new number on fingers and act out one more in songs and stories.
assessment: Check whether each child adds one more to a group of one to three and says or shows how many now.
expectedOutcomes: Adds one more to a group of one to three.
Shows how many now with fingers.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: asking politely for more

lessons.title: One more block
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will add one more block to a small group and say how many now.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, give one to each friend and say more and same.
lessons.starter: Put two blocks on the tray and ask "How many?" Add one block and say "One more block. Now how many?" Count together.
teacherActivities: Start with one block and count it. Add one more and say "One more. Now two."
Start with two blocks, add one more and say "One more. Now three." Count again.
Ask a child to add one more to a group of three and say how many.
Play "One more, please" with the children asking for one more block.
learnerActivities: Children count one, two with you.
Children count to three and say "three".
Child adds one block and counts to four with help.
Children say "one more, please" and add a block.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Start with one block and count it. Add one more and say "One more. Now two." Children: Children count one, two with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Start with two blocks, add one more and say "One more. Now three." Count again. Children: Children count to three and say "three".
Step 3. Teacher: Ask a child to add one more to a group of three and say how many. Children: Child adds one block and counts to four with help.
Step 4. Teacher: Play "One more, please" with the children asking for one more block. Children: Children say "one more, please" and add a block.

practical.title: One more tray
steps: Give each pair a tray with two blocks.
Swap and try again with three blocks.
practical.safety: Use blocks larger than a child’s fist; keep trays on the floor; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Start with one block and add one more with hand-over-hand help.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to add one more to four blocks and say how many.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks now?
questions.expected: The correct number after adding one.

expectedOutcomes: Adds one more to a small group
lessons.conclusion: Count the final group aloud and say "One more, one more, well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Add one more spoon or one more shoe to a pile at home and count.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "add one more block to a small group and say how many now" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A block added to a group
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: One more block, one more block, count them all, one more block.

lessons.title: One more finger
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show one more finger and say the new number.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, give one to each friend and say more and same.
lessons.starter: Show one finger and say "One." Raise another finger and say "One more finger. Now two."
teacherActivities: Hold up two fingers and say "Two." Add one more finger and say "Three."
Call "Show me three." Then say "Add one more" and hold up four fingers.
Play "one more" game: show a number and ask for one more.
Ask pairs to take turns: one shows fingers, the other shows one more.
learnerActivities: Children copy and say the numbers.
Children add one finger and say "four".
Children show one more finger and say the new number.
Pairs play and say the numbers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up two fingers and say "Two." Add one more finger and say "Three." Children: Children copy and say the numbers.
Step 2. Teacher: Call "Show me three." Then say "Add one more" and hold up four fingers. Children: Children add one finger and say "four".
Step 3. Teacher: Play "one more" game: show a number and ask for one more. Children: Children show one more finger and say the new number.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask pairs to take turns: one shows fingers, the other shows one more. Children: Pairs play and say the numbers.

practical.title: Finger one more
steps: Sit in pairs facing each other.
One shows two fingers; the partner shows one more.
practical.safety: Keep hands away from faces; sit comfortably; the leader stops the game if it becomes loud.

differentiation.support: Use one and two fingers only with an adult adding the finger.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show one more than four fingers using both hands.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is one more than two?

lessons.conclusion: Fold the fingers away and say "One more, one more, sleep."
lessons.homeConnection: Play "one more" with your child using fingers while waiting.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show one more finger and say the new number" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: One more fruit in the basket
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: One more in stories and songs
objectives: Children will add one more toy fruit to a basket and count how many now.
successCriteria: Recounts and says how many now
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, give one to each friend and say more and same.
lessons.starter: Put two toy fruits in the basket and cover them with a cloth. Say "Two fruits. One more fruit comes into the basket. Now how many?"
teacherActivities: Add one fruit while the children watch. Lift the cloth and count.
Cover the basket again and add another fruit. Ask "How many now?"
Give each child a turn to add one fruit to the basket.
Take one fruit away and ask "Now how many?"
learnerActivities: Children count the fruits and say "three".
Children guess, then count to check.
Child adds one fruit and the group counts.
Children count and say the new number.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Add one fruit while the children watch. Lift the cloth and count. Children: Children count the fruits and say "three".
Step 2. Teacher: Cover the basket again and add another fruit. Ask "How many now?" Children: Children guess, then count to check.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a turn to add one fruit to the basket. Children: Child adds one fruit and the group counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Take one fruit away and ask "Now how many?" Children: Children count and say the new number.

practical.title: Fruit basket one more
steps: Start with two fruits in a basket.
practical.safety: Use toy fruits larger than a child’s fist; keep baskets on the table.

differentiation.support: Start with one fruit and add one more with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to add one more twice and say how many.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many fruits now?
questions.expected: The correct number after adding one.

questions.question: What happens if I take one away?

expectedOutcomes: Adds one more to a basket
lessons.conclusion: Count the fruits in the basket one last time and say the number.
lessons.homeConnection: Count items in a bowl and add one more each time.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "add one more toy fruit to a basket and count how many now" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The hungry caterpillar friend
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: One more in stories and songs
objectives: Children will listen to a story about adding one more and act it out.
successCriteria: Says one more at the right moment
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, give one to each friend and say more and same.
resources: A soft toy caterpillar or a green cloth
lessons.starter: Show the caterpillar toy and say "Little Caterpillar is hungry. He eats one more leaf each day. Let us count his leaves."
teacherActivities: Tell the first day and feed one leaf to the caterpillar. Say "One leaf."
Feed one more leaf and ask "How many now?"
Feed another leaf and ask the same question.
Let each child feed the caterpillar one more leaf while the group says the number.
learnerActivities: Children say "one" and munch.
Children count and say "two".
Children count and say "three".
Child feeds a leaf and says "one more".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the first day and feed one leaf to the caterpillar. Say "One leaf." Children: Children say "one" and munch.
Step 2. Teacher: Feed one more leaf and ask "How many now?" Children: Children count and say "two".
Step 3. Teacher: Feed another leaf and ask the same question. Children: Children count and say "three".
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child feed the caterpillar one more leaf while the group says the number. Children: Child feeds a leaf and says "one more".

practical.title: Feed the caterpillar
steps: Give each pair a caterpillar and three leaves.
Feed one leaf at a time.
practical.safety: Use toy or paper leaves; keep them away from mouths; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Feed only two leaves and say the numbers with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the story with four leaves.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many leaves did he eat on Tuesday?
What did he say after the third leaf?

expectedOutcomes: Adds one more in a story
lessons.conclusion: Put the caterpillar to sleep under a cloth and say "Goodnight."
lessons.homeConnection: Tell the caterpillar story at home using beans or buttons for leaves, held by an adult.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen to a story about adding one more and act it out" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Munch, munch, munch, one more leaf. Munch, munch, munch, now we have two.
learnerFacing.story: Little Caterpillar was hungry. On Monday he ate one leaf. Munch! On Tuesday he ate one more leaf. Now he had eaten two. Munch, munch! On Wednesday he ate one more leaf. Now three! Munch, munch, munch! Little Caterpillar was full. He rolled up and went to sleep.

lessons.title: One more stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can add one more at three stations.
successCriteria: Adds one more to a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to five with support, give one to each friend and say more and same.
lessons.starter: Sing the one more song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Add one more" and "How many now?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child adds and says the number.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Add one more" and "How many now?" Children: Child adds and says the number.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use large objects only; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be the "one more" leader.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: adds one more to a group of one to three; says or shows how many now.

questions.question: How many now?
questions.expected: The correct number after adding one.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Sing the one more song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise one more at home with fruit or blocks.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can add one more at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
